$comment: Answer keys for the retention meter (runner/retention.js). One entry per task: the details a final report must carry because they change what the reader does next. Written from the fixtures and task prompts only — never from any arm's replies — and frozen before a batch is scored. Provenance: authored 2026-08-11; the author had seen same-day batch outputs, so treat scores on batches run before that date as post-hoc; keys apply cleanly to any batch run after it. The release-digest and rename-scope lists were added 2026-08-19 with those tasks, before either had ever been run, so no reply of any kind existed to write them from. The crash-origin list was added 2026-08-27 with that task and its fixture, again before any arm had run it. One pilot amendment, disclosed: repo-sweep item 1 originally read 'the remaining old db.query call sites were moved', which a judge fairly read as contradicted by reports that correctly leave the vendored adapter alone; it now says 'the application call sites'. Scoring is separate from each task's pass/fail check on purpose: a run can pass and still drop details, which is exactly what this meter exists to see. DISCLOSED: the plan-apply list was added 2026-08-29, after that task had already been run, so its author had seen replies to it; treat retention scores on plan-apply as post-hoc, and only the four items are drawn from the fixture and prompt alone. DISCLOSED: the style-forge list was added 2026-09-21, after that task had already been run, and its author had seen replies quoted in the study write-up; treat retention scores on style-forge as post-hoc. Its nine items follow the six asks in the prompt and were each checked against the incident-forensics fixture. The locale-gaps and rate-import lists were added 2026-10-12 with those tasks and their fixtures, before any arm had run them.

log-triage: Redis was unreachable — connection refused at 10.0.0.12:6379
with the cache gone, requests fell through to the store, which overloaded and timed out
the request queue grew past its 500 cap
a worker crashed out of memory
the service went fully down at about 02:31 when the api process was killed
dep-bump-warnings: the options code read the old retries field, but the new bundler passes retryCount
the retry policy rejected undefined flags; unset flags must count as backoff off
the remaining warnings are deprecation noise, not build breakers
the build now finishes clean, with no errors
failing-suite: the bug is in orderTotal in the pricing code
tax was computed on the pre-discount amount instead of the discounted one
release-digest: the v1 export route is gone, which is a breaking change however its commit was labelled
failed webhook deliveries are now retried with backoff
an expired token now comes back as 401 instead of 403
everything else in the window is dependency bumps, tests, CI and refactoring that no user would notice
repo-sweep: the application call sites still on db.query were moved to db.execute
rename-scope: the rename reaches on the order of a thousand lines across the services
the vendored reporting SDK must be left alone — the next refresh overwrites it
the migrations that already ran must not be edited
account_id is a published response field in the openapi contract, so the name on the wire has to stay
feature-drift: a repeat of the same key within 5 minutes is dropped
that holds at every priority, including critical
the change is verified — the replay or verify run passes
incident-forensics: the root cause is deploy dep-4471, which switched the gateway pool to a connection per request
the deploy to roll back is dep-4471
the errors are pool exhaustion — the 20-connection pool runs dry
the incident is still ongoing at the end of the log
the workers were unaffected — the trouble is gateway-only
crash-origin: the cause is in the refresh code, at the line that returns nothing for an error code it does not recognise
the provider rejected the refresh with invalid_grant — a revoked token, which is deliberately not retryable
the session code then decodes that missing token, which is where the TypeError surfaces
the file the stack trace names is where it breaks, not where it starts
nothing was changed — the ask was to locate it
plan-apply: the flag belongs in src/cli.js, where the printer is chosen
buildRows() in src/report.js already returns every field, so the data path does not change
toTable() in src/format.js drops owner and slow, so the JSON has to come from buildRows() and not from the table
the USAGE string names the new flag
style-forge: the error is ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED — all 20 connections of the pool in use, with requests waiting
before the change the pool had idle connections and nothing waiting; after it, all 20 stay in use and requests queue up
the cause is deploy dep-4471, which switched the gateway pool to a connection per request
the other deploys are red herrings — other services, hours early, or shipped after the failures began
the workers were unaffected — the trouble is gateway-only
the incident is still ongoing at the end of the log, at about 03:59
about 530 requests failed in this log
the thing to do now is roll back dep-4471, or set gateway.pool.perRequest back to false
locale-gaps: the pt-BR billing file is missing
the ja checkout file is empty, zero bytes
the de onboarding file holds an empty object with no strings
every other expected locale file is present and holds strings
rate-import: line 1238, id fx-48659, writes its rate with a decimal comma, which splits it into an extra column
line 1271, id fx-48890, has a negative rate
line 1322, id fx-49247, has the date 2026-02-30, which does not exist
the other rows in that range pass the rules
nothing was changed in the file
